@davidkna 
I have also updated the docs in the meantime... Pls take a look at them as well.
This enum is no longer necessary with a shared base config.
Given the common config struct, the module can use the regular `module` function approach.
Some of these extensions appear to be very unusual.
Given the potential overlaps, this module should be disabled-by-default or ensure (`!`-patterns) that they are mutually exclusive.

Regarding these extensions they are simply all the recognised c++ extensions as per gcc's manual. 

Should I trim this down to just the widely used extensions?

I didn't properly understand this point.

are you asking me to make a CommonConfig struct out of this trait and use it somehow??

I have removed it and updated the code right now.
I think that's a good idea since this amount could break the table in the docs, but if you feel strongly about leaving it as-is should be fine.
I am satisfied with how it turned out now.
I have updated this to most commonly used c++ extensions
